q: How do I get a student job with no experience?

Start with jobs that offer training, such as cafes, shops, events and school support. Show what you can already do: volunteering, clubs, sport, group projects and caring for family all count. Apply to several jobs at once, and apply early in the day, as many shifts are filled fast.
What should go on a student CV?

Keep it to one page. Put the days and hours you can work near the top, then your course, any work or volunteering, and two or three skills with a short example each. Use our free UK CV template to start.
What happens at a part-time job interview?

Most are short and friendly, often 15 to 20 minutes, sometimes with a trial shift. Expect questions about when you can work, how you would deal with a busy customer and why you want the job. Arrive a few minutes early and bring ID that shows your right to work.
When and how will I get paid?
Most part-time jobs pay weekly, every two weeks or monthly, straight into your bank account. You have a legal right to a payslip that shows your pay and any tax or National Insurance taken off.
Do I get paid holiday?
Yes. Part-time, casual and zero-hours workers all build up paid holiday. Ask your employer how they work it out and how to book it.
Can I turn down shifts during exams?
On a zero-hours or casual contract you can usually say no to shifts. Tell your manager your exam dates early, and update the hours you can work when your timetable changes.
How do I spot a fake job?

Never pay for training, a uniform or a DBS check up front. Be careful if an employer only talks to you on WhatsApp or Telegram, offers very high pay for easy work, or asks for bank details before an interview.
How often are new student jobs added?
Every morning. Jobs older than 30 days, or that have closed, are taken off, so everything you see is current. Save the jobs you like so you can find them again.

Parents.h: Going back to work as a parent: common questions
q: How do I explain a career break on my CV?

Add one honest line, such as "Career break to raise my family, 2019 to 2025". Then list what you did in that time that shows your skills: volunteering, school committees, courses or running a busy household. Employers see career breaks all the time.
Can I ask for flexible or part-time hours?

Yes. Every employee can make a formal request for flexible working from their first day in a job, up to twice a year, and the employer must decide within two months. It is a right to ask, not a right to get it, so it helps to say how the hours would work for the team.
What does term-time only mean?
You work during school terms and have the school holidays off. Many term-time jobs spread your pay evenly across the whole year, so check the advert or ask how the pay is worked out.
What help is there with childcare costs?

In England, eligible working parents can get 30 hours of funded childcare a week, 38 weeks a year, for children from 9 months up to school age. Tax-Free Childcare adds £2 for every £8 you pay, up to £2,000 per child a year. Check what you can get on GOV.UK.
Will working affect my Universal Credit?

Your Universal Credit goes down gradually as you earn more, so most people are better off in work. If you get Universal Credit you may also claim back up to 85% of your childcare costs. Use a benefits calculator on GOV.UK to check your own case.
What if my child is ill and I have to stay home?
Employees have the right to reasonable time off to deal with an emergency involving a dependant, such as a sick child, from their first day. It is usually unpaid, so check your contract.
How do I spot a fake work-from-home job?
Never pay for a starter kit, training or software. Be careful of jobs that promise high pay for little work, only talk on WhatsApp, or ask you to receive money or parcels for someone else.

Newcomers.h: Working in the UK for the first time: common questions
q: How do I prove I can work in the UK?
British and Irish citizens show their passport. Most other people share a right-to-work code from GOV.UK. The code starts with W and lasts 90 days. The employer checks it before your first day.
Do I need a National Insurance number to start?
No. You can start work before it arrives if you can prove your right to work. Apply for it free on GOV.UK and give it to your employer when you have it.
Will my overseas qualifications count?
Many employers accept them. UK ENIC can give you a statement that shows how your qualification compares to UK ones. It is a paid service, so check whether the job needs it before you pay.
How is a UK CV different?

Keep it to two pages at most. Do not add a photo, your date of birth or your marital status. Start with a short summary, then your work history with the newest job first. Our free CV template follows UK style.
My English is not perfect. Can I still apply?

Yes. Many entry-level jobs in cafes, warehouses, cleaning and care train you on the job. Local colleges and councils run English (ESOL) classes, often free or low cost, which you can do alongside work.
Am I paid the same as everyone else?
Yes. The minimum wage, paid holiday and payslips apply to every worker in the UK, whatever their nationality. If you are paid less than the minimum wage, you can report it to GOV.UK.
How do I spot a job scam?

Real employers never ask you to pay for a job, a visa or a DBS check before an offer. Never send your passport or bank details before a real interview, and be careful of jobs offered only on WhatsApp or Telegram.
What is an apprenticeship?

A real, paid job where part of your working time is spent training towards a recognised qualification. You learn on the job and with a college or training provider, and you never pay for the training.
Who can do one?
Anyone aged 16 or over in England who is not in full-time education. There is no upper age limit, so they suit school leavers and adults changing career.
Do I need A levels?

Not always. Level 2 and 3 apprenticeships often ask for GCSEs, and some take people with none. Higher and degree apprenticeships usually ask for A levels or a Level 3 qualification. Each advert lists what it needs.
When should I apply?

Many apprenticeships start in September, and big employers often open applications in the autumn and close them in early spring. Others start all year round. Check the closing date on each advert and apply early.
How much will I earn?
At least the apprentice rate of £8.00 an hour if you are under 19 or in your first year. After that you get the minimum wage for your age. Many employers pay more.
How do I tell a real apprenticeship from a fake one?

A real apprenticeship is a paid job with an employer. Be careful of "apprenticeships" that are really courses you pay for, or that offer no wage. You can check adverts on GOV.UK Find an apprenticeship.
What is the difference between a graduate scheme and a graduate job?

A graduate scheme is a structured programme, often one to three years, with training and rotations, and fixed application dates. A graduate job is a normal entry-level role you can apply for any time of year. Both are good starts.
When do graduate schemes open?
Many large employers open in the autumn for jobs starting the next September, and some close early once they have enough applicants. Smaller employers hire all year.
Will employers accept a 2:2?
Many do, and more employers now look at skills rather than degree class. Check the entry requirements on each advert.
Should internships be paid?
If you are doing real work as a worker, the law says you must get at least the minimum wage. Be careful of unpaid internships that are really jobs.
When do I start repaying my student loan?
Repayments start from the April after you leave your course, and only when you earn over your plan's threshold. They are taken from your pay automatically.
What happens at an assessment centre?
Usually a mix of group tasks, an interview, a presentation and written exercises. Employers look at how you work with others, not just the right answers.

Experienced.h: Experienced and professional roles: common questions
q: What does FTE mean in a salary?
Full-time equivalent. It is what the job would pay for full-time hours. If the role is part-time, you get a share of that figure based on your hours.
Why do some jobs say area approximate?
Some adverts only say London or give a wide area. We place them in the most likely borough and mark them so you know to check the exact location in the advert.
Are these jobs from agencies?
Some are. Jobs come from official job feeds, which include adverts from employers and recruitment agencies. Each advert shows who is hiring. We remove adverts that ask for fees or look like scams.
Can I ask for flexible working in a new job?
Yes. Every employee can make a formal flexible working request from their first day, up to twice a year, and the employer must decide within two months.
How fresh are the jobs?
New jobs are added every morning, and jobs older than 30 days are removed, so every job here was posted recently.
Can my company advertise here?
Yes, for free. Use Post a job. Every advert is checked by a person before it goes live.
